To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a subviral RNA (satC) that is associated with Turnip Crinkle virus (TC) has evolved a ribosome binding translase enhancer (TSS) derived from the helper virus (TCV) (2) the TSS is required for satC to accumulate in infected plants, and (3) the satC TCV-derived TSS is a target of selection in infected plants.

a subviral satellite RNA of TCV, satC, contains a ribosome binding translative enhancer that was derived from TCV, that this ribosome binding transliterative enhancer is not essential for satC replication, and that the TSS in satC has evolved to a conformation that is less likely to bind to the ribosome than the original TCV-derived TSS.
the helper virus-derived, TCV TSS, is a translational enhancer that evolved from the TSS of satC, and that the evolution of satC was influenced by both the helper virus and host.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evolution of an RNA structure in the 3’ UTR that is involved in the replication of the subviral RNA, SatC.

the evolution of a helper virus derived translational enhancer that binds to 80S-ribosomes and is required for efficient replication of a subviral satellite RNA.
how RNA structure and function can be modified by a helper virus to facilitate its own replication and transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the satC TCV TSS region is not a ribosome-binding translational enhancer but that the TCV TSS is.
TSS of TCV and satC are similar but not identical, and the TSS of satC is not a functional equivalent of TSS of TSV.

a helper virus-derived ribosome binding site in an untranslated subviral satellite RNA has evolved to become nonfunctional, but that a nonfunctional TSS-like sequence has been maintained in satC, possibly for reasons of RNA structure and/or replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
satC evolved a TSS region that binds ribosomes poorly and that this region has been conserved in the satC of other TCV isolates.
the TCV TSS evolved from a ribosome binding enhancer to a ribosome binding repressor.

TCV and satC evolved from a common ancestral RNA, but TCV retained a TSS that enhanced its replication, and satC lost the TSS and evolved a novel structure that enhanced its replication in a TCV-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TSS is an RNA element that evolved to bind ribosomes and that the satC TCV sequence has been modified to reduce ribosome binding.
the TSS is an ancient RNA structure that evolved to enhance translation of viral RNA.
TSS-like structures can evolve to bind ribosomes and that this process can be reversed.
